claims.text: One call (query w013, Vanilla top 30, S4) took 10,749 s before it returned a normal reply.
claims.source: Windows System event log: Kernel-Power 105 power source change 2026-11-23 17:00:32, Kernel-Power 42 entering sleep 17:00:40, Kernel-General 1 time jump of 10,702,275 ms at resume 19:59:22. Raw block qwen3_4b/vanilla+r30tfidf/test3/S4_o0.json: w000-w012 took 49.6 s after the S3 block's last save (16:59:43), so w013 started about 17:00:33; 17:00:33 + 10,749 s = 19:59:42, 20 s after resume; the remaining 86 calls took 835.5 s and the S4 file was last saved 20:13:40 (matches). So about 10,702 of the 10,749 s were the laptop asleep; the run was paused, not stopped, from 17:00 to 19:59.
claims.fix: "One call (query w013, Vanilla top 30, S4) spanned a sleep of the laptop from 17:00 to 19:59 (Windows event log) and returned a normal reply after 10,749 s of wall-clock time."
claims.auditor_verdict: The number is right (10,749.36 s, a normal 5-ID reply), but the sentence reads as a slow model call; it was a laptop sleep during the call. The paragraph also presents 21:16 as the only interruption.
